items.title: ci(#7089): re-arm production-line-guard + opencode-config-guard for main; grandfather 7 over-limit files
items.body: Executes Drew's #7089 ruling (2026-11-11 01:23 CST, #7089 comment 6789768080): enable all the jobs for the main branch, re-enable the manually disabled ones, retire what makes no sense — merge queues stay disabled. Worked under queue task 11349 (triage of #6959). ## Live findings first (the 2026-11-07 audit was stale for five of the seven) Already armed on main — **no change**: mcpx-fix-test-guard, go-modules-build, identity-build, map-build, mcpx-nixbuild (all active, push[main] path-gated + pull_request + dispatch). Actually dark, fixed here: - **production-line-guard** — was `workflow_dispatch`-only. Restores the full pre-sweep trigger shape (pre-`5a94833ea3`): push to main + pull_request, both path-gated on `pkgs/**`, `apps/**`, and the guard files. This is #6959's own acceptance shape. - **opencode-config-guard** — was `disabled_manually` with an ungated pull_request leg and no main trigger. Adds push to main (unfiltered, per its pre-sweep shape and the ci-policy prose that promises it), restores the #1401 path gate on the pull_request leg, extended to the workflow's current check set (route-rules + provider-catalog fixtures postdate the original gate). `merge_group` omitted: there is no merge queue (Drew ruling 2026-11-08, recorded in ci-policy.md). The venue is re-enabled via the Actions API immediately after this merge lands. ## Agreement bookkeeping (#7089 contract) - Both recorded waivers deleted in the same PR, as the contract requires: `opencode-config-guard.yml|main|6953` and `production-line-guard.yml|pr|6959` (checker script + ci-policy waiver table). The waiver set is now empty. - ci-policy: production-line guard row gains its restored main tier; the opencode-config-guard prose no longer promises merge groups; the stale "disabled_manually" parenthetical is corrected. ## Line guard lands green The grandfather list was empty and the guard failed on 7 files already over the 2,500 limit. Each is grandfathered in `check-production-line-limit.sh` with a linked split issue, per the guard's own convention (an entry is deleted in the same PR that lands its split): client.rs #8588, turso_queue.rs #8589, serve.rs #8590, directory.rs #8591, actor.rs #8592, core.rs #8593, world_session/mod.rs #8594. ## Local evidence - `bash .github/scripts/check-ci-policy-agreement.sh` → OK (10 workflows, 0 waived disagreements); its contract tests pass. - `bash .github/scripts/check-production-line-limit.sh` → PASSED, 7 grandfathered warnings naming their split issues; its contract tests pass. ## Nonsense audit All 61 workflow files on main inventoried. No file met the unambiguous-retire bar (every file has a live target and a distinguishable job); the arguable list and the four registered-but-fileless workflow entries (build.yml, cargo-target-janitor.yml, yard-reaper-tests.yml, zz-var-write-probe.yml — registry residue that cannot fire) are recorded on #7089 for a ruling instead of being deleted on a lane's read. Refs: #7089, #6959, #6953, #6929, #6981. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: feat(ci): guard against new root *COMPLETE* / *SUMMARY* status files (#12136)
items.body:
Refs #12136 — the guard slice. **#13047 (the removal slice) merged 2026-11-24 as `4bf439c9d9a`**, so this PR is no longer stacked: it has been brought onto current main and retargeted to `main`. The guard is now green on main's tree.

This replaces the closed PR #13060 (closed automatically when its stacked base branch was deleted on merge). Same three files, carried forward unchanged except the schedule-registry row, which is now merged against main's current Surface 4 table.

## What this adds

- `.github/scripts/check-root-status-files.sh` — fails, naming each offender, when a file at the repository root has a name containing `COMPLETE` or `SUMMARY` (case-insensitive). Root only: the same names inside a directory (e.g. the `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/` copies) are untouched. Strict one-optional-positional argument contract per #3352.
- `.github/scripts/check-root-status-files.test.sh` — contract tests in the check-fleet-lock.test.sh style (fixture roots in a temp dir).
- `.github/workflows/root-status-guard.yml` — nightly + dispatch venue modeled on production-line-guard.yml, running the guard and its contract tests.
- `.github/test-suite-registry.json` — new `ci.root-status-files` suite row, mirroring `ci.production-line-limit`.
- `check-ci-policy-agreement.sh` + `.github/ci-policy.md` — the new workflow joins the #7089 agreement registry as a nightly guard, with its policy table row.
- `doc/fleet-schedule-registry.md` — Surface 4 row for `root-status-guard` (daily 07:17 UTC matching the workflow cron), surface count 3 → 4. This closes the one review finding from the Codex review on #13060 (P1: register the new schedule).

## Evidence (run on this branch after merging main)

```
$ bash .github/scripts/check-root-status-files.sh
root-status-guard: checked 113 root files
root-status-guard: OK

$ bash .github/scripts/check-root-status-files.test.sh
ok: a clean root passes (nested *COMPLETE* is out of scope)
ok: a root TASK_COMPLETE.md fails, naming the file
ok: a lowercase root *summary* file fails
ok: a root SLICE1_COMPLETION_SUMMARY.txt fails
ok: a root *STATUS*-only name passes (guard covers *COMPLETE* / *SUMMARY*)
ok: a missing root fails
ok: an extra argument is a usage error (exit 2, usage printed)
check-root-status-files.test: OK
```

Fails-before (from the original PR, against the pre-removal tree `cb4c54ced`): guard exits 1 naming 16 root *COMPLETE* / *SUMMARY* files.

## Merge Danger

Low. One new bash guard, its fixture-based contract test, one nightly workflow that only runs the guard, and registry rows. No runtime path changes; the workflow is nightly/dispatch only.

Scheduled-workflow note: the new nightly workflow is registered in `doc/fleet-schedule-registry.md` Surface 4 in the same pass, per AGENTS.md.

items.title: fix(ci-policy checker): verify push branches: [main] for the main tier (#7950)
items.body: Closes #7950. The ci-policy agreement checker (PR #7945, #7089 Phase 1) enforced the main tier by trigger *name* only: any `push` satisfied the leg, though the pinned contract in `.github/ci-policy.md` is a push on `branches: [main]`. A push that can never run on main was certified as agreeing — and for waived workflows flipped to **STALE WAIVER**, ordering the waiver deleted in the same PR (the issue's probe cases 1–4 reproduce exactly this, ending in a false `ci-policy-agreement: OK`). **Fix** (`.github/scripts/check-ci-policy-agreement.sh`): - New `push_targets_main` reads the push trigger's own sub-keys from the workflow's `on:` block — `branches`, `branches-ignore`, `tags` in both flow-list (`branches: [main]`) and block-sequence forms, alongside the existing bare/scalar/flow trigger forms. - The main leg now agrees only when the push actually targets main: bare/unfiltered `push:` still counts; an explicit `branches:` filter must list `main`; `branches-ignore:` naming `main`, a `branches:` list without `main`, and a tags-only push keep the leg in disagreement — reported as WAIVED against its recorded waiver (with a message that names the mis-targeting), or as a DISAGREEMENT when unwaived. Never stale, never certified. - No workflow triggers, tiers, or waivers change; the named-equivalent-venue clause is untouched (it's a prose disposition, not tree-checkable). **Tests** (`.github/scripts/check-ci-policy-agreement.test.sh`, 5 → 11 cases, fixtures now carry real trigger sub-keys): - `branches: [release]`, `branches-ignore: [main]`, and tags-only pushes keep mcpx-nixbuild's waived main leg WAIVED and the tree green — not STALE. - `branches: [main]` in flow and block-sequence forms satisfies the leg (waiver correctly stale). - An unwaived main leg (`mcpx-fix-test-guard`) with `branches-ignore: [main]` fails as a DISAGREEMENT. - The existing 5 contract tests pass unchanged, and the checker stays green on the current-main tree with the recorded waiver set unchanged (10 waived disagreements). --- 🤖 agent-note:v1 — queue task 14311 (lane code-g). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Chores** * Improved CI policy checks to verify that main-tier workflows’ push triggers include `main`, including when branch filters are configured. * Updated validation to distinguish workflows that lack a push trigger from those whose filters exclude `main`.

items.body: **Rename the Jules-era workflow files + the remediation label for what they do now** — Drew's order, main chat 2026-11-11: "Rename and reword all of these for what they do now." All three workflows STAY; they are named honestly now. Jules was decommissioned in #5098; nothing here was backed by it anymore. ## Old → new | Before | After | What it is | |---|---|---| | `.github/workflows/jules.yml` | `.github/workflows/pm-dispatch.yml` | The pm-dispatch hub (workflow name was already `pm-dispatch`): fires tracked OpenCode sessions from GitHub events — label-triggered remediation, the Monday 04:00 UTC cleanup cron, manual dispatch | | `.github/workflows/jules-daily-codebase-ideation.yml` | `.github/workflows/daily-codebase-ideation.yml` | Daily 06:00 UTC dispatched session: codebase review, ideation, gap analysis, triage | | `.github/workflows/jules-daily-flake-sync.yml` | `.github/workflows/daily-flake-sync.yml` | Daily 05:00 UTC dispatched session: Nix config optimization + dependency auditing | | label `jules` | label `dispatch/remediate` | "Hand this issue to remediation" — applied by main-broken under its 3-concurrent budget; renamed via the labels API immediately after this merge so the 3 open issues carrying it keep their hold under the new name | ## What changed - `git mv` renames (history follows); header comments and prose reworded so nothing describes the dead Jules service as current. The retired-package guard in the ideation workflow keeps its path data (its job is to detect those packages returning) with reworded messages; its prompt already pointed at `pkgs/fleet` and now says so without the Jules framing. - Every live reference updated: `main-broken.yml` (coin spec, apply/budget/release logic, timeline filter, agent-note holder tokens now `holder: dispatch`), `repo-sweeper.yml`, `nix-ci.yml`, `.github/ci-policy.md` (retention rationale rewritten), `.github/actionlint.yaml` (ignore paths), roadmaps, `doc/agent-stack-notes.md`, `scripts/classify_failure.py` comment. - Behavior identical: same triggers, schedules, permissions, inputs and defaults (the flake-sync legacy input's description is reworded but keeps its "ignored" semantics, which its own wiring verifier keys on). ## Label inventory (why renaming it in this PR is safe) All live references to the remediation label are in this repo: the hub's trigger condition, main-broken's coin/apply/release logic, ci-policy + sweeper prose. The pm-dispatch starter action (`.github/actions/pm-dispatch-start`) has no label reference; the laptop pm-dispatch config has none; the fleet worker runbooks have none. The aggregator's `jules` session-source taxonomy, the `source/jules` + `app/jules*` labels, and the `.jules/` Bolt/Palette persona journal paths are different things (historical session provenance) and are deliberately untouched — inventoried on #7089. ## Verification (local, on this tree) - YAML parses for all 7 touched workflow/config files. - `.github/scripts/check-ci-policy-agreement.sh` — OK (10 workflows, 0 waived disagreements); its contract tests pass. - Both dailies' embedded verifier steps run green against the renamed files (input wiring, retired-package guard, default-branch guard). - Grep read-back: no living reference to the old filenames; hub triggers byte-equivalent except the label name. Merge note: checks will sit queued behind the Actions backlog purge ordered tonight; merging on the local verification above, per the same standing pattern as PR #8596. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR?
